headline: 5 Essential Items Every Cross-Border Wedding Guest Must Now Carry Under The New 'Customs of Affection' Protocol
body:
1. A notarized three-generation family tree printed on waterproof paper to ensure no one at the reception is actually a lost distant cousin from a rival neighborhood.
2. A portable 'Vibe Authenticator' device that checks if the wedding playlist is sufficiently nostalgic to bypass regional security sensors.
3. A collection of ten 'emergency anecdotes' regarding mild traffic inconveniences, pre-approved by immigration authorities to fill awkward silences during the Sangeet.
4. A set of diplomatic-grade confetti launchers, calibrated to exactly 45 degrees to ensure no stray glitter drifts into restricted airspaces during the festivities.
5. A dual-currency wedding gift box that automatically calculates the tax liability for both nations before the bride even steps onto the stage.
caption: Planning a wedding across the border? Make sure you check your pockets for the mandatory 'Vibe Authenticator' before hitting the dance floor. Don't let your RSVP turn into an international incident! #WeddingSeason #Customs #Diplomacy (satire)
igHook: Would you survive a border-crossing wedding with only these five items in your carry-on?
imagePrompt: A wide-angle, slightly blurry shot of a crowded, festive wedding tent at dusk, with strings of fairy lights overhead and a large, ornate golden metal gate standing strangely in the middle of the dance floor.

sourceHeadline.title: After Operation Sindoor visa hurdle, 150 Pakistani brides reach India

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 manages to inject true absurdity (Vibe Authenticator, diplomatic confetti launchers) while maintaining a deadpan tone. It avoids the repetitive 'notarized affidavit' tropes that saturate the other entries, offering the most creative and visually evocative take on the bureaucratic theme.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses whimsical, satirical bureaucracy to comment on wedding culture and geopolitical absurdity without naming real public figures, private individuals, or targeting specific religions, castes, or ethnicities. The image prompt is generic and free of restricted identifiers.
